comment.narrative: 79 of the tested water is free from fecal contamination at the baseline

The endline results showed that 86.14 of respondents have increased access to safe and affordable water without experiencing any difficulties compared to the baseline results which showed that only 12.6 had safe access and affordable water. Overall 98.74 of respondents confirmed an increased access to safe and affordable water which includes the original 12.6 of respondents who reported having safe access and affordable water at the baseline. The increased access of the targeted population to safe water in regards to quality and quantity can be traced back to several factors including the restoration of the targeted desalination plants and the filling points that now supply drinking water to the ten targeted communities. Another factor that contributes to this increased access in terms of access and affordability is the constant availability of water trucks within these communities providing safe and affordable drinking water according to WHOPWA standards for drinking water at a reduced cost. In addition according to the interviews with community committee leaders conducted during the project evaluation process the cost of one cubic meter of drinking water was reduced by 20 30 at the targeted private desalination plants while the water quality and quantity were monitored on a regular basis by members of the community committees. Overall 86.14 of targeted men women and children have increased access to safe and affordable water denoting that the target indicator of 50 was surpassed by 36.14.
